intro: A 3-inch topper of medium-firm memory foam or natural latex is the best mattress topper for most people, because it cushions shoulders and hips without letting the spine sink out of line. Here are seven worth buying, and the one problem no topper can fix.

A topper changes how the top few inches of a bed feel. It does not change what is underneath. Buy one to soften a mattress that is too firm, to add a little support to one that is slightly too soft, or to cool down a foam bed, and skip it if your mattress already dips in the middle.

sections.h: Which Mattress Topper Should You Buy?

blocks.p: Buy the ViscoSoft Select High Density if you want one topper that suits most beds. It is 3 inches of gel memory foam that ViscoSoft lists at 3.1 lb/ft³, with corner straps, a washable cover and a medium-firm feel.

Side sleepers who want the deepest cushion should look at the Tempur-Pedic TEMPUR-Adapt + Cooling, which Tempur describes as extra-soft. For back pain, or a mattress that has gone a little soft, the firm Pure Green Natural Latex is the one topper here built to add support rather than cushion.
On a budget, the Linenspa 3 Inch Gel and the Zinus 3 Inch Green Tea still add a real comfort layer. For a pillow top, the Sleep Innovations Dual Layer stacks fiber on gel foam for 4 inches in total.

One warning. A topper changes the top few inches of your bed. It cannot rebuild support that a worn-out mattress has lost. If your mattress has a visible dip, a topper will follow it, and the money is better spent on a new bed from our [best mattress guide](/best-mattress/).

sections.h: How Do the 7 Mattress Toppers Compare?

blocks.p: The table compares the seven on the specs that decide how a topper feels. Figures come from maker pages and retailer listings. Where a maker does not publish a number, we leave it out.
The feel column tells you whether a topper will soften or firm your bed. Only the Pure Green latex in medium or firm is designed to add support. Every memory foam topper here makes a bed softer.

The anchoring column matters more than people expect. A strapless topper relies on friction and its own weight, and owners commonly report straightening them every few days. If that bothers you, buy one with straps.
Topper warranties cover manufacturing defects, not the gradual softening every foam goes through. Check today's price on each, since topper prices swing widely during sales.

sections.h: Memory Foam, Gel, Latex or Fiber: Which Topper Material Is Best?

blocks.p: The material sets how a topper feels, how warm it sleeps and how long it lasts. The best one depends on the problem you want fixed.

Memory foam softens under body heat and pressure, so it molds around shoulders and hips. The trade-offs are heat and a slow rebound that can feel stuck when you turn over. Gel foam is memory foam with gel beads or swirls mixed in. Makers say the gel draws heat away, and it can feel cooler at first, but it still hugs.

Latex is springier. It pushes back instead of sinking slowly, which makes it easier to move on and better at adding support. Natural latex breathes better and usually outlasts foam. It is also heavy: Pure Green lists its firm latex at 5.9 lb/ft³.

Fiber toppers are quilted pads of polyester fill. They feel cloudy and sleep cool, but they add almost no support and compress over time. Use fiber to make a firm bed cozier, or as a layer over foam, as the Sleep Innovations Dual Layer does.

sections.h: How Thick Should a Mattress Topper Be: 2, 3 or 4 Inches?

blocks.p: Thickness controls how much of the mattress you still feel. More is not automatically better, because a thick soft layer lets heavier body parts sink out of line.

head: Thickness
What It Does
Best For
rows: Clear change in feel without deep sink
Side sleepers on a hard bed

blocks.p: For most people, 3 inches is right. It cushions a side sleeper's shoulder on a firm mattress while the mattress underneath keeps doing the support work.

Go thinner if you sleep on your back or stomach, because those positions need the hips level with the shoulders. Go to 4 inches only if you sleep on your side, the mattress is genuinely hard, and you are on the lighter side.

blocks.h3: Density: the number most toppers leave out

blocks.p: Foam density, in pounds per cubic foot, is the best clue to how long a foam topper will hold its shape. Few budget makers publish it, which is why ViscoSoft's 3.1 lb/ft³ stands out. Density is not firmness: dense foam can feel soft, and light foam can feel firm when new, then break down quickly.

Heavier sleepers compress a topper more every night, so they should weight density more heavily. If you need a new bed instead, our guide to mattresses for heavy people covers beds built for more weight.

sections.h: Can a Topper Make a Mattress Firmer or Softer?

blocks.p: Softening is easy. Firming is hard. Almost every topper makes a bed feel softer. Only a few can make a soft bed feel firmer, and even those have limits.

This is the job toppers do best. A 2 to 3 inch layer of memory foam or soft latex adds pressure relief to a mattress that feels like a board. If your bed is supportive but too hard, that is the cheapest fix there is.

A firm latex topper can make a slightly soft mattress feel more supportive. Pure Green recommends its firm grade for this, at least 2 inches and preferably 3. Its firm latex is rated at a 25 percent IFD of 46 lbf, against 20 lbf for its soft. Memory foam toppers, even ones labeled firm, rarely firm up a bed.
THE RULE
A topper cannot fix a sagging mattress.

If your mattress has a visible body impression or you roll toward the middle, a topper will drape into that hollow and your spine will follow. Replace the mattress, and check its warranty first, since many cover impressions past a stated depth.

Test before you spend. Strip the bed, lay a broom handle across the mattress, and look for a gap where you sleep. A gap means the support layers are worn out, and the topper money belongs toward a new mattress.

sections.h: What Is the Best Mattress Topper for Back Pain?

blocks.p: For back pain, the best mattress topper keeps your spine in a neutral line, and that is rarely the softest one. Look for medium to firm latex, or medium-firm foam 2 to 3 inches thick, on a mattress that is still supportive.

Latex pushes back against the heaviest part of the body, usually the hips, which helps keep the lower back from bowing into the bed. The medium or firm Pure Green is our pick. The medium-firm ViscoSoft is the foam alternative.

Skip thick, soft memory foam if you sleep on your back or stomach and wake up sore. A deep soft layer lets the hips sink below the shoulders. The plush Sleep Innovations and the extra-soft Tempur-Adapt are excellent for side sleepers and the wrong choice here.

A topper is not a treatment. If back pain lasts more than a few weeks or comes with numbness or leg pain, see a doctor or physical therapist. If the mattress has lost support, our guide to the best mattress for back pain covers firmness by position and when a new bed is the better fix.

sections.h: What Is the Best Mattress Topper for Side Sleepers?

blocks.p: Side sleepers need the opposite. Lying on your side loads a narrow shoulder and hip, so the surface has to give enough for both to sink in while the waist stays supported. On a firm mattress, a 3-inch memory foam topper adds exactly that.

The Tempur-Pedic TEMPUR-Adapt + Cooling is our side sleeper pick, and owners commonly report that it relieves shoulder pressure on hard beds. Tempur lists the queen at $519 at the time of writing, though Amazon has often discounted it. The Sleep Innovations and Lucid are cheaper routes.

blocks.h3: Side sleepers with hip or shoulder pain

blocks.p: A numb arm or sore hip on waking usually means the mattress pushes back too hard at those points, and a soft 3 or 4 inch topper is the usual fix. Soft latex, which Pure Green rates at 20 lbf, is the cooler alternative to memory foam.

Side sleepers with back pain should choose a 3-inch medium topper rather than a 4-inch plush one. If the mattress is the real problem, see our guide to the [best mattress for side sleepers](/best-mattress-for-side-sleepers/). Older sleepers who struggle to turn on slow foam may prefer latex, a point our guide to [mattresses for seniors](/best-mattress-for-seniors/) covers.

Many do. Memory foam closes around you, which cuts airflow at the surface, and owners of plain foam toppers commonly report sleeping warmer than on the bare mattress. Gel, vents and covers help by different amounts.

Latex sleeps cooler than memory foam, and fiber cooler still. Among foam toppers, Lucid's ventilation holes and ViscoSoft's airflow channels are designed to move heat out. Lucid rates its own gel topper 3 out of 5 for cooling, an honest signal that vents help without solving the problem.
A cool-to-the-touch cover like the Tempur's feels cool when you lie down, and that fades as the fabric warms. Neither will fix a hot bedroom.
If you sleep very hot, choose latex or a fiber-topped design, keep the topper thin, and use cotton or linen sheets.

sections.h: How Do You Keep a Mattress Topper From Sliding?

blocks.p: A topper that creeps off the edge every night is one of the most common complaints. The fixes are cheap.

The ViscoSoft has elastic corner straps and a beaded mesh base. Retail listings describe straps on the Tempur-Adapt too. The Sleep Innovations cover wraps the mattress edges and holds both layers together. The Linenspa, Lucid and Zinus have no straps.

Use a deep-pocket fitted sheet that covers mattress and topper together. Measure first: a 10-inch mattress plus a 3-inch topper needs at least a 13-inch pocket. A zippered topper cover, a protector over both layers, or a non-slip rug pad underneath all add grip.
Check the mattress too. A topper slides more easily on a mattress that is itself slipping on its frame, so fix that first.

mistakes: Buying a topper to fix a sagging mattress

A topper drapes into whatever is under it. If your mattress has a visible dip or you roll toward the middle, a topper will follow that hollow and your spine will too. Check for sagging with the sheets off first, and replace a worn-out mattress instead.
Buying the thickest, softest topper for a bad back

A 4-inch plush topper feels wonderful in the store and can leave a back or stomach sleeper's hips sinking below the shoulders. For back pain, choose medium to firm latex or a medium-firm foam at 2 to 3 inches. Save the plush 4-inch toppers for side sleepers on very firm beds.

A 3-inch topper adds 3 inches to the height of your bed. A fitted sheet that fit the mattress alone will now pop off the corners and let the topper slide. Measure the mattress and topper together and buy deep-pocket sheets deep enough to fit both.
Expecting a memory foam topper to make a bed firmer

Memory foam softens under body heat, so even toppers labeled firm usually make a mattress feel softer. If you need more support, buy a firm latex topper, which the maker of the Pure Green recommends at 2 inches minimum and ideally 3 inches. Anything softer will only add cushion.
Judging the topper on the first night

Compressed foam toppers need time to expand fully, and Zinus asks that you unbox its topper within 72 hours. New foam can also smell for a day or two. Give a topper a week before deciding, but check the return window first, since many cannot be returned once used.
bottomLine: A mattress topper is worth buying when your mattress is supportive but feels wrong on top. For most beds, the ViscoSoft 3 Inch Select High Density is the one we would choose first, with the Tempur-Adapt + Cooling for side sleepers who want the deepest cushion and the Pure Green firm latex for sore backs. Do not buy any topper to rescue a mattress that sags. Check for a dip with the sheets off, and if you find one, spend the money on a new bed instead. Whatever you choose, measure for deep-pocket sheets, and give it a week before you decide.

faqs.q: What is the best mattress topper?
faqs.a: For most people, the ViscoSoft 3 Inch Select High Density. ViscoSoft lists its gel memory foam at 3.1 lb/ft³, describes the feel as medium-firm, and adds corner straps and a washable cover. Side sleepers should consider the Tempur-Adapt + Cooling, and anyone with back pain should try a firm latex topper.

faqs.q: What is the best mattress topper for back pain?
faqs.a: A medium or firm natural latex topper about 3 inches thick, such as the Pure Green, is the best mattress topper for back pain on a supportive bed. Latex pushes back against the hips and helps keep the spine level. If pain persists for weeks, see a doctor or physical therapist.

faqs.q: What is the best mattress topper for side sleepers?
faqs.a: A soft 3-inch memory foam topper, such as the Tempur-Pedic TEMPUR-Adapt + Cooling, is the best mattress topper for side sleepers on a firm mattress. It lets the shoulder and hip sink in while the waist stays supported. Soft latex is the cooler alternative if memory foam feels too warm.

faqs.q: Is a 2 or 3 inch mattress topper better?
faqs.a: A 3-inch topper suits most people because it changes the feel of the bed noticeably without letting the hips sink too far. Choose 2 inches if you sleep on your back or stomach, or if your mattress is only slightly too firm. Go to 4 inches only as a side sleeper on a hard mattress.

faqs.q: Can a mattress topper fix a sagging mattress?
faqs.a: No. A topper follows the shape of the mattress under it, so it will sink into a dip just as you do. It can soften a firm bed or slightly firm a soft one, but it cannot restore worn-out support. If your mattress has a visible dip, check its warranty and plan on replacing it.

faqs.q: Is latex or memory foam better for a mattress topper?
faqs.a: It depends on what you want. Memory foam contours closely and relieves pressure, which side sleepers like, but it sleeps warmer and feels slow to move on. Latex is springier, cooler and usually more durable, and firm latex can add support. Latex also costs more. For back pain, it usually has the edge.

faqs.q: How do I keep my mattress topper from sliding?
faqs.a: Buy a topper with corner straps or a grippy base, like the ViscoSoft, if sliding would bother you. For a strapless topper, use a deep-pocket fitted sheet that covers the mattress and topper together, a zippered topper cover, or a non-slip rug pad underneath, and check that the mattress itself is not sliding.
